name: validate_oco_tpsl_for_submit
doc:
FFI-exposed OCO TP/SL submit gate. Runs the SAME directional TP/SL
validation the order-attach path uses (buy-SL-trigger-too-high /
sell-SL-trigger-too-low / TP-direction checks → CDKeys
`pr_trade_function_input_sl_higher_value` / `_lower_value` etc.) so the
Kotlin modify (amend) submit gate can block a bad order BEFORE it reaches
the backend — matching online iOS, which validates here.

This is a thin UniFFI twin of the internal
[`validate_oco_tpsl`][Self::validate_oco_tpsl]: it forwards the exact same
7 inputs and returns the same [`OKTTpslValidationResult`]. It adds ZERO
validation logic of its own — `validate_oco_tpsl` reads `side` /
`order_price` / `is_amend` / trigger-px-type from the kernel state (seeded
by `apply_side` / `update_context_pricing` / `set_amend_mode` /
`set_trigger_px_type`) and the market price via `resolve_market_price`
(session ticker → `seed_amend_market_price` override). Additive surface;
no other Interactor contract changes.

The returned record carries `is_valid` plus the per-leg error CDKeys
(`tp_error_code` / `sl_error_code`) and the missing-field markers; the
Kotlin binder resolves those CDKeys through the canonical resolver and
blocks the submit when `is_valid == false`.

Monotonic counter bumped on EVERY chase-value / max-chase-value input action.

Kernel-internal, no Kotlin reader (the `_internal` suffix is on the R-MIG-284
default whitelist). It exists so clamping an over-bound input back onto the SAME
bound still changes the state and therefore still notifies: without it
`modify_state`'s equality dedup swallows the notification, no render runs, and the
controlled input keeps the raw over-bound text -- the failure mode hit by
AdjustLeverage (2026-05-30) and attached-TPSL trailing (2026-07-19).

Deliberately NOT reset by lifecycle orchestration: a monotonic counter must never
go backwards, or a post-reset value can collide with a pre-reset one and re-arm the
very dedup hole it exists to close.

doc:
R1a — render-ready projection of the SINGLE take-profit leg currently being
EDITED in the V1 `MultipleTpSettingFragment` "set multiple TP" dialog.

# Why this is separate from `PureContractMultiProjection`
`PureContractMultiProjection.tp_legs` is the LIST of already-CONFIRMED legs
(V1 `multiplePriview` preview recycler). This struct is the EDIT FORM above
it (V1 `tpView` + `estimateAmountLl` + the progress row) — the not-yet-added
leg the user is typing, plus the "set-pct / remaining-pct" progress. Splitting the
two mirrors the V1 layout (one editable form + one confirmed list) and lets
the Kotlin pure sheet stop computing `calcEstimateAmount` itself (V1
`MultipleTpSettingFragment.calcEstimateAmount:374` uses the Kotlin
`TradeAvailableManager` + `TradeUnitUtils` — an A1 violation). Every numeric
value here is produced by the clean `OKTTpslMultiManager` /
`attach_facade` calculator, never recomputed in Kotlin.

- `estimate_amount`  ← `calcEstimateAmount:374` (`estimateAmountTv`)
- `estimate_profit`  ← per-leg `profit` (`profitTip.result` / ByPrice PnL
bubble) — `UniSetTpSlView.getMultipleTpPriceInfo:1836`
- `set_percent`      ← `priceSettingInfo.totalPercent` (set-pct)
- `left_percent`     ← `getLeftPercent():449` = `1F.subS(totalPercent)` (remaining-pct)
- `is_full`          ← `isFull():441` = `totalPercent.gte(1)`
- `is_estimate_visible` ← `estimateAmountLl.isVisible:358`
- `is_limit_kind` / `trigger_px_type` ← shared `isTPLimit()` /
`tpTriggerPriceType` (V1 keeps ONE type for the whole multi-tp session —
`showTpTriggerPriceTypeDialog` writes it, `getCallbackResult` applies it to

doc:
Typed capability for the order-detail header's "go to trade" entry.

One value answers both questions the hosts used to answer separately: should
the entry be visible, and where would a tap go. `Unavailable` means "no entry
AND no action", so a host cannot render a dead affordance; `Available` carries
a target that is ready by construction.

Both shells used to decide this in the native layer by comparing
`header.instType` against `"CONVERT"` (Android `PureOrderDetailUtils`
`isConvert`, iOS `showsGoToTrade`), and then assembled the destination from the
loaded VO with a launch-argument fallback. That left two real gaps:

* a blank or unrecognised `instType` passed the CONVERT test, so the entry
rendered and the tap silently did nothing;
* "which identity wins" was a per-host convention rather than a contract.

Rust now decides: the entry exists only for a recognised, tradable business
line on a HYDRATED order, and the identity is always the hydrated order's own.
The launch argument is deliberately NOT a fallback — the header this entry
lives in is itself built from the hydrated VO, so "no VO" already means "no
entry", and preferring the launch value could only ever navigate somewhere the
detail is not about.

A host may still AND-suppress the entry when it has no local navigation
capability; it must never re-enable what this says is unavailable.

NOT modelled yet, pending the product answers the report calls out: whether
`SPOT` + full/partial liquidation offers the entry (today's Android behaviour
is kept: it does), whether buy/sell side changes the landing, instrument
availability, the expired FUTURES/EVENTS same-series fallback, the EVENTS
outcome, and a typed unavailable reason.

doc:
Clip a clicked depth quantity by the current max-available via the
shared `ClipDepthClickQuantityUseCase`. Returns the clipped quantity (or
empty when not applicable). The instrument context is resolved from the
parent session.

# Known limitation — `max_avail` is `None` for non-PM accounts

`ClipDepthClickQuantityUseCase` short-circuits to an empty string for
every non-portfolio-margin account when `max_avail` is `None` (it needs
the live `MaxAvailResponse` to know the clip ceiling — see the
`let Some(..) = max_avail else { return String::new() }` arms in
`clip_depth_click_quantity_use_case.rs`). Today this interactor cannot
reach a live max-available value **synchronously**:

- `MaxAvailableManager` is stateless — its `fetch()` is `async` and does
a network round-trip; it caches no "latest" snapshot.
- `TradeSessionContext` exposes no max-available accessor / cached value.
- `PureDepthInteractor` owns no `MaxAvailableManager` subscription and
has no max-available state field of its own (unlike the sibling
spot-limit pure interactor, which subscribes + caches the response in
its own state via `fetch_max_available`).

Because this is a **synchronous** FFI getter (`-> String`), it cannot
`.await` a fetch. Feeding the real value therefore requires net-new
infrastructure (a depth-owned max-available subscription that caches the
latest `MaxAvailResponse` into the interactor's state, or a
session-level cached snapshot), not a one-line wiring change. Until that
lands, `max_avail` stays `None` — PM accounts clip correctly (the use
case returns the raw qty directly for PM), non-PM accounts get the
empty-string fallback that already shipped. Tracked for follow-up; do
not fabricate a sync max-available source here.

fields.name: markers
fields.doc:
Tooltip rows for EVERY sampled x, ascending, aligned with the sampled positions the
series are built from.

The chart library snaps a highlight to an actual plotted vertex, so the native side
looks the tooltip up by that x and renders it in the SAME frame. Reporting the touch
back to Rust and waiting for a new frame instead left the tooltip one async hop behind
the finger — blank on first touch, and showing the previous x throughout a drag —
where native computes it inline (`markerValuesAt`, `MmrImrVariablesFragment.kt:1509`).

The xs are already lot-aligned by the sampler, so this needs no separate snapping step:
looking up a plotted x IS native's snap-down-to-lotSz result.

fields.name: x_tick_precision
fields.doc:
Precision the native side formats axis ticks at: the decimal places of the
instrument's `lotSz`, which is the position-size step.

# Why no tick positions or labels

Tick PLACEMENT belongs to the chart library, not here. Native leaves the x
positions to MPAndroidChart on purpose - the Figma's 0 / 10,000 / 50,000 / 100,000
are laid out space-between and carry no positional meaning, so reproducing them
would invent a precision the design does not have - and caps only the density
(`setLabelCount(5, false)`, deliberately unforced, because forcing divides the
range evenly and yields 20.4 / 40.8 instead of the intended 20 / 40).

Since the library decides WHICH values to label, Rust cannot pre-format them. What
it can own is the unit and the precision, which is exactly what crosses here: the
native formatter renders whatever value it is handed, as a percent or a bare
multiple per [`Self::axis_is_percent`], at this precision.

name: recompute_spot_per_leg_pnl
doc:
Per-leg (TP / SL) by-price PnL for the estimated-profit rows. Bug fix
(2026-06-23): the binder used to render the single merged `pnl_display`
under BOTH the TP and SL rows, so they always matched. This getter
returns each leg's own earn (TP from the TP trigger, SL from the SL
trigger). Only `ByPriceStrategy` overrides the strategy method; other TP
kinds return `has_per_leg = false`, and the binder then keeps the single
`pnl_display`. Purely additive — `compute()` is untouched.

Bug (a) fix (2026-06-24): when the user enters ONLY the change-rate
(percent) box — not the trigger box — `s.input.tp_trigger_raw` /
`sl_trigger_raw` are empty, so `compute_spot_per_leg_pnl` produced `None`
for both legs and BOTH estimated-profit rows were hidden ("enter the
change-rate first -> neither leg shows"). The merged `pnl_display` path already handled this (see the
BUG-A fix at the end of `apply_by_price_rate_linkage`: it derives the
trigger px from the percent and re-runs the PnL), but this per-leg getter
reads `s.input` directly and bypasses the linkage. Mirror that here: run
the rate→trigger linkage to obtain the derived `tp_trigger_px` /
`sl_trigger_px`, then feed a `derived_input` (with the derived triggers
back-filled into `tp_trigger_raw` / `sl_trigger_raw`) into the strategy so
each leg shows its own earn whether the user entered the trigger directly
OR derived it from a change-rate. V1 parity: `ByPriceSpPresent` always
runs `setCalculate*TriggerPx` (percent → trigger) THEN
`showProfitAndLoss()`, so the tip uses the derived trigger.

PRIVATE (spec/interactor.md §D): the math/linkage is unchanged but this
is no longer an FFI compute-verb getter. It is the worker behind the
`update_spot_per_leg_pnl` action — the result is projected into State
and read by the UI via [`state`][Self::state]. Math is 1:1 with the
former `compute_spot_per_leg_pnl()` getter; only the trigger site
(action) and result sink (State) moved.
